explanations.answer: Allure her and speak to her tenderly
explanations.explanation: That's the one, baker. The LORD says, "…I will allure her and lead her to the wilderness, and speak to her tenderly." After all that hard talk, I was ready for a slammed door. Instead the next thing out of His mouth is a soft voice, and I had to read it twice.

explanations.answer: Leave her to wander on her own
explanations.explanation: Not quite, friend. The LORD says He will lead her to the wilderness, so He's the one doing the leading. And He doesn't go quiet on her. He says He will speak to her tenderly. Wandering off alone is more my style when I'm hunting for a lost oven mitt.

explanations.answer: Hand her back over to her lovers
explanations.explanation: No, baker, that's not in this promise. The LORD says, "…I will allure her…" so He's the one doing the drawing. He doesn't mention handing her to anyone else. This verse turns toward her, not away from her.

Yes, baker, vineyards! Earlier the LORD talked about taking things away (Hosea 2:9-12). Now, in the wilderness, He says, "There I will give back her vineyards…" Taking is one thing, but giving back is a whole different promise.

Close to the kind of thing, but that's not the one, friend. In this verse the LORD says He will give back her vineyards. Jewelry isn't mentioned here. I'd have made the same guess, and my whole wardrobe is a hat, an apron and a neckerchief.

Not this time, baker. Silver isn't what the LORD names in Hosea 2:15. He says, "There I will give back her vineyards…" Vineyards are what He promises to return, and they're what you want to hold onto for this one.

That's right, baker. Achor is where Achan was stoned (Joshua 7:24-26), after he took things he was told not to take (Joshua 7:1; 7:20-21). And the LORD says He will make that same valley "…into a gateway of hope." He takes a place with a heavy name and gives it a brand new label.

I see why you'd say that, friend, since the valley has a hard history. Achan was stoned there (Joshua 7:24-26), after he took things he was told not to take (Joshua 7:1; 7:20-21). But the LORD says He'll make it "…a gateway of hope." He's not putting up another warning sign.

That would match the old story of the valley, but it isn't what He says. Achor is where Achan was stoned (Joshua 7:24-26), after he took things he was told not to take (Joshua 7:1; 7:20-21). The LORD says He'll turn it "…into a gateway of hope." He is changing it, not repeating it.

True, baker! The LORD says, "There she will respond as she did in the days of her youth, as in the day she came up out of Egypt." He points back to the day she left Egypt and says she'll answer Him that way again. I think that's a sweet memory to hand somebody.

Not false, friend. The LORD says, "There she will respond as she did in the days of her youth, as in the day she came up out of Egypt." So He does point to that day. It's a true statement, and a tender one.
That one's flipped, baker. The LORD declares, "you will call Me ‘my Husband,’ and no longer call Me ‘my Master.’" So it's the other way around. Husband is the name she'll use.
Right, friend, it's false. The LORD says, "you will call Me ‘my Husband,’ and no longer call Me ‘my Master.’" The card had the two names swapped around, and you caught it.

Yes, baker. The LORD says, "…I will remove from her lips the names of the Baals; no longer will their names be invoked." The Baals were false gods her lips had been calling on. He says He'll take those names right out of her mouth.

Nice try, friend, but complaining isn't what He names here. The LORD says He will remove "…the names of the Baals…" from her lips. The Baals were false gods. Complaints aren't mentioned, though I admit I've grumbled at a stubborn batch of dough.

explanations.answer: The songs of their old feasts
explanations.explanation: That's not in the verse, baker. What the LORD says He'll remove is "…the names of the Baals…" and He says no longer will their names be invoked. The Baals were false gods. Songs aren't mentioned.

explanations.answer: The beasts and birds and crawling creatures
explanations.explanation: That's the surprise guest list, baker! The LORD says, "…I will make a covenant for them with the beasts of the field and the birds of the air and the creatures that crawl on the ground." Animals are named right alongside the promise. I'd be shocked too, and I once got startled by my own mustache.

explanations.answer: The kings of the nations around them
explanations.explanation: That would be the usual kind of agreement, friend, but it's not what He says. The LORD says He'll make a covenant "…with the beasts of the field and the birds of the air and the creatures that crawl on the ground." No kings are named. The other side of this deal is the animals.

explanations.answer: The priests who served the Baals
explanations.explanation: No, baker. The LORD already said He'll remove the Baals' names from her lips, and no priests show up in this covenant. He makes it "…with the beasts of the field and the birds of the air and the creatures that crawl on the ground." Creatures, not clergy.
That's it, baker. The LORD says, "…I will abolish bow and sword and battle in the land…" The weapons go, and the fighting goes with them. It's the kind of cleanup I'd happily volunteer for.

I get the thinking, friend, since those protect a place. But the LORD doesn't say that here. He says, "…I will abolish bow and sword and battle in the land…" The weapons and the fighting are what He names.

Good guess for a big list, baker, but it's not this one. The LORD says He will abolish "…bow and sword and battle in the land…" Kings and crowns aren't in the verse. He's talking about the weapons and the war.

True, baker! After abolishing bow and sword and battle, the LORD says, "…and will make them lie down in safety." Picture lying down with the fighting gone from the land. I haven't rested that easy since my days on a nice flat counter.

It's actually true, friend. The LORD says He'll abolish bow and sword and battle in the land, "…and will make them lie down in safety." The safety goes right along with the battle ending. Don't let a short sentence like that slip past you.
Careful, baker, the LORD says something bigger. He says, "So I will betroth you to Me forever…" Forever is a lot longer than a season. That one word changes the whole card.
That's right, friend. The LORD says, "So I will betroth you to Me forever…" No season in that word. Forever means forever, and that's why this one is false.

Yes, baker. The LORD says, "And I will betroth you in faithfulness, and you will know the LORD." The betrothal and the knowing are right next to each other. I think there's something good in that pairing.

explanations.answer: Build a house for the LORD
explanations.explanation: Not in this verse, friend. After saying He'll betroth them in faithfulness, the LORD says, "…you will know the LORD." Building a house isn't mentioned. Knowing Him is the promise.
That's a big promise, baker, but it's not the one here. The LORD says, "…you will know the LORD." Nothing about ruling nations shows up in this verse. Knowing Him comes first.

That's it, baker. The LORD says, "And the earth will respond to the grain, to the new wine and oil…" It's a whole chain: heavens, earth, then grain, wine and oil. I'd love a chain of command in my bakery that smooth.

I'm partial to stars, friend, since I've got a sky full of them. But this verse says, "…the earth will respond to the grain, to the new wine and oil…" The earth answers what grows from it. Grain is the word for this blank.

Reasonable guess, baker, but rivers aren't named here. The verse says, "And the earth will respond to the grain, to the new wine and oil…" Grain is what the earth answers. Keep following the chain, because there's one more link after it.
True, baker! The LORD says, "…I will have compassion on ‘No Compassion.’…" The very name that said no compassion gets compassion. I like how that name takes a turn.
It's true, friend. The LORD says, "…I will have compassion on ‘No Compassion.’…" That's right there in the verse. Yes, the name gets the very thing it said was missing.
Yes, baker. The LORD says, "I will say to those called 'Not My People,' 'You are My people.'" The name said one thing and He says the opposite. I'd frame that sentence if I had a wall.

explanations.answer: You may live near My people
explanations.explanation: That's a smaller promise than the one in the verse, friend. The LORD says, "I will say to those called 'Not My People,' 'You are My people.'" He doesn't say they can live nearby. He calls them His own.
That's not what the verse says, baker. The LORD says to those called "Not My People…" "You are My people…" Serving isn't mentioned. They become His people.

That's the answer, baker. The LORD says, "You are My people…" and then they say, "You are my God." He speaks first, and they answer Him back. It's the last line of the passage and it's a good one to end on.

I can see why that might come to mind, friend, but it's not in the text. After the LORD says "You are My people…" the verse says they will say, "You are my God." That's the whole answer they give here.
That's not what they say here, baker. When the LORD calls them His people, the verse says they will say, "You are my God." Nothing about a king shows up. They answer Him as their God.
